newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil privatization draws mass protest, violence.
newsitem.headline: Brazil privatization draws mass protest, violence.

text.p: Demonstrators protesting over Latin America's largest privatization plan clashed with riot police in downtown Rio de Janeiro on Tuesday, witnesses said.

About 1,000 youths and trade unionists trying to break through a security cordon protecting the Rio stock exchange threw stones and cans at police in riot gear. Police returned fire with tear gas, stun grenades and water canon.
Globo television said at least two people were injured by thrown stones.

A $5 billion sell-off of state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) set for Tuesday was delayed by a series of court injunctions issued across the country. It was unclear when the auction, due to begin with the sale of up to 45 percent of voting shares, would begin.

The privatization, the biggest so far in Latin America, has sparked considerable opposition. Critics, who accuse the government of selling off Brazil's mineral wealth cheaply to foreigners, range from former presidents Jose Sarney and Itamar Franco to all of the country's Catholic bishops.

Trade unions had vowed to bus at least 5,000 protesters into Rio's city center for a mass protest against the sale. Six hundred and fifty police were drafted to protect the stock exchange from the demonstrators and a square in front of the exchange was fenced off.
